inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E (year ends 2026-10-31): 9M actual $32,192M (10-Q Q3 FY2026) + Q4 guidance midpoint $14,350M (range $13.9-14.8B, press release 2026-09-02). Ties to the raised FY26 growth guide of 34-37% on FY2025 $34,296M. FY2026 is the first full year of Juniper (closed 2025-07-02); the +35% is acquisition step-change, not organic.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 (10-Q, 1,449M) vs 1,336M basic. The 113M gap is the if-converted 7.625% Series C mandatory convertible preferred (30M pref shares, $1.5B, converts ~Sept 2027, ~76M common at the minimum rate) plus ~37M RSUs/options. Because the preferred is inside the diluted count it is NOT in net debt; its remaining ~1 year of dividends is a bridge item. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Buybacks resumed ($447M 9M FY2026 vs $202M FY2025) and mgmt plans to return >=75% of Q4 FCF, so the flat count is being funded.
inputs.net_debt_note: Consolidated, balance sheet 2026-07-31: total debt $20,244M (XBRL DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount; LT $17,343M + current $2,901M) less cash $6,216M. Of the debt, $11.6B is 'debt benefiting Financial Services' (FY2025 10-K, 7.0x on $1.7B FS equity, against $13.2B net portfolio assets). The interest on that debt ($500M FY2025, us-gaap:FinancingInterestExpense) is a cost line ABOVE earnings from operations, i.e. already inside the EBITDA the flows are built from, so that debt is added back in equity_bridge net of FS cash ($727M) rather than deducted twice. Operating leases ($1.7B liability) are NOT added to debt (lease cost stays in opex; one treatment).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026E on HPE's own definition (OCF less net capex, i.e. PP&E/software purchases less proceeds from sale of PP&E, FX-adjusted): guidance 'at least $3.75B' raised 2026-09-02; 9M actual $2,581M. This is a LEVERED figure (after ~$1.1B of cash interest) and after Juniper integration cash costs, so it sits well below the unlevered component-built year-1 owner FCF; the gap is after-tax corporate interest (~$0.5B), integration/cost-reduction cash (~$0.35B) and the SBC/withholding charge that HPE's FCF omits. DB-basis FCF (OCF less gross capex) is 9M $2,332M; FY2025 $627M.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-Q Q3 FY2026 cash flow statement: stock-based compensation add-back $599M for 9M (FY2025 $643M) plus taxes paid related to net-share settlement of equity awards $338M for 9M in financing activities (FY2025 $289M). Annualised with FY2025's Q4 seasonality (Q4 SBC ~$215M, Q4 withholding ~$60M because HPE's vests cluster in Q1): FY2026E SBC $815M + withholding $400M = $1,215M, 2.6% of FY2026E revenue. HPE publishes no combined figure in its non-GAAP reconciliation, so the two lines are summed. Withholding has doubled with the share price (vest-date value vs grant-date expense), which is exactly the cost the add-back misses.
inputs.interest_income_note: Net-debt company (net debt 14.0B vs FCF base ~2.6B), so interest income is not stripped. FY2025 interest income was $406M on the pre-close cash pile ($14.8B at FY2024); cash is now $6.2B. Interest income sits in 'Interest and other, net' below operating income, so it is not inside the EBITDA the flows are built from either way.
inputs.buyback_cash_note: 9M FY2026 repurchases $447M (FY2025 $202M, FY2024 $150M). Dividends $568M 9M plus $87M preferred.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-28T20:04:53Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 19.84-65.65
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Standard build: Rf 4.2% (10y UST), beta 1.15, ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity 10.0%; pre-tax cost of debt 5.0% (BBB), after-tax 3.9%; ~18% debt weight -> 8.9%, rounded 9.0% (the 2026-09-29 first build). SANITY-CHECK FIX (Step 8c.5 priority 2), explicit premium components added: cyclicality +0.50pp (AI-systems revenue is tied to a capex cycle that can pause; HPE's own FY2018-24 organic revenue CAGR is -0.4% and pre-SBC EBITDA margin ranged 9.5-17.6%), regulatory/integration +0.25pp (Tunney Act state-AG review of the DOJ Juniper settlement, export controls on AI systems, $600M synergy execution), supplier concentration +0.25pp (GPU/HBM allocation from a single supplier gates AI-systems deliveries). WACC = 10.0%. Cross-check: HPE's observed beta since the Juniper close is ~1.3-1.4, which alone gives cost of equity 10.7-11.2% and WACC ~9.7-9.9%, so 10.0% is what the market-implied beta says before any premium. Same WACC in all three scenarios: the premium is structural, and scenario risk is still charged once through paths and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (ASC 842 liability $1.7B at FY2025) stay as an operating cost inside EBITDA; lease liabilities are not added to net debt. One treatment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, US filer). HPE is a US enterprise IT hardware/networking company; the adaptations file was not needed (USD/USD, leases immaterial, NCI immaterial) except for the captive-finance point handled in the bridge. First valuation of this ticker. DISCONTINUITY: the $14B Juniper acquisition closed 2025-07-02, so FY2025 (4 months of Juniper, $458M acquisition costs, $500M+ restructuring, GAAP op loss) and FY2026 (+35% revenue, record 40.4% non-GAAP GM in Q3) are both non-representative in opposite directions. The margin driver is anchored to management's FY2027 framework (non-GAAP op margin 14-15%) rather than to the FY2025 loss or the Q3 FY2026 record quarter. EBITDA DRIVER DEFINITION: pre-SBC EBITDA = GAAP earnings from operations + D&A + SBC + transitory Juniper acquisition/integration charges; the recurring cost-reduction/restructuring programme (a near-annual feature at HPE) is treated as a real cost, not added back. Cross-check: FY2026E non-GAAP OP ~$6.7B (9M $4,584M actual; FY guide +100-105% on FY2025) + depreciation ex-intangible-amortisation ~$2.2B = ~$8.9B = 19.2% of FY2026E revenue; FY2027 guide 14-15% + ~4.3% depreciation = 18.3-19.3%, less ~0.3% normalised restructuring -> base year-1 18.5%. D&A is 7.5% of revenue today because Juniper added ~$1.26B/yr of intangible amortisation (mostly non-deductible, which is why the cash tax rate on EBIT is set above HPE's 15% non-GAAP rate); the da_pct path tapers toward the ~5% underlying depreciation as that amortisation runs off. Capex is NET of proceeds from sale of PP&E (HPEFS recycles lease equipment): 9M FY2026 $1,897M gross less $288M proceeds = 5.0% of revenue. Working capital: hardware/finance-receivables business, receivables + inventory > payables (deferred revenue $5.6B helps but does not flip the sign); capture set at -6% of the revenue change. YEAR-1 SANITY: base FY2027 unlevered owner FCF ~$4.6B (8.7% of revenue) vs HPE's own FY2027 FCF floor of >=$5.0B; bridging (+$1.4B SBC/withholding HPE excludes, -$0.5B after-tax corporate interest HPE deducts) puts the model ~10% above the floor, which is a guidance floor, not a midpoint. Preferred dividends ($116M/yr until the Sept-2027 mandatory conversion) are a bridge deduction. Known DB issue for the parent: core_metrics total_debt for FY2024 (22,402) and FY2025 (26,357) double-counts the current portion vs XBRL combined debt (18,246 / 22,365); Q1-Q3 FY2026 rows are correct and this build uses Q3 FY2026. SANITY-CHECK FIX PASS 2026-09-29 (one pass, per research-stock Step 8c.5): the first build tripped on implied P/B 3.00x (10yr max 1.28x) and EV/EBITDA 57.2x (10yr max 31.6x). The EV/EBITDA trip is a denominator artefact: the check divides by FY2025 GAAP EBITDA less SBC ($2,300M - $643M = $1,657M), a year with a GAAP operating loss (-$437M), $458M of Juniper acquisition costs, $500M+ restructuring and only four months of Juniper; FY2025's own historical print of 31.6x at one-third of today's price is the same artefact. On FY2026E pre-SBC EBITDA (~$8.9B; ~$7.7B post-SBC) the original build implied ~12x, inside the 10.8x average band. The P/B trip is partly structural (HPE earned 5-10% ROE on book for a decade and traded at 0.7-1.3x; post-Juniper mid-cycle owner FCF is ~$4B unlevered on ~$27B book) but the diagnosis 'peak_fcf' was right about the margin path: the base plateau of 19.5% pre-SBC EBITDA was 2pp above HPE's best standalone year (FY2023 17.6%) and 4.7pp above the post-spin median (14.8%). Fixes applied, in priority order: (1) mid-cycle margins - base plateau 18.0% (FY2023-24 standalone ~17.4% + Juniper mix/synergy net of AI-server dilution), bull 20.0%, bear 15.0% (post-spin median); (2) WACC 9.0% -> 10.0% with named premium components (see wacc_rationale); (3) growth - the guided FY2027 year (14%, contracted $5.9B AI backlog) is kept because it is evidence, but the fade now reverts to HPE's clean through-cycle organic rate: FY2018->FY2025 revenue CAGR +1.5% (FY2018->FY2024, pre-Juniper, -0.4%); base 5/3/2.5 then 2.0% terminal (was 8/5/4/3.5 to 2.5%); the -4.2% 'through-cycle CAGR' in the trip spans the FY2014-16 HP Inc / DXC / Micro Focus basis break and was not used; (4) exit-multiple caps in EV/EBITDA terms per scenario (see exit_multiple_cap block) - all non-binding because the Gordon terminal values already sit at 5.4-8.5x post-SBC EBITDA, below the 10yr average of 10.8x; the 15x FCF cap remains the tighter constraint. Result: implied EV/EBITDA on the check's FY2025 denominator falls inside the 1.5x-max bound; implied P/B falls to ~2.1x, still above the 1.93x bound (1.5 x 1.28x). It was NOT forced lower: doing so would require valuing the post-Juniper company at the ROE of the pre-Juniper value-trap decade, and the model already sits ~35-40% below the market price on a mid-cycle, through-cycle-growth, 10%-WACC basis. See sanity_check_response.
inputs.mid_cycle_fcf_note: Levered owner FCF (HPE-definition FCF less SBC less net-share withholding) at mid-cycle for the COMBINED entity: HPE standalone owner-FCF median FY2018-25 ~$1.3B (sanity_check median 1,306) + Juniper standalone owner FCF ~$0.5B (FY2024 FCF ~$0.85B less ~$0.3B SBC) + after-tax synergy ~$0.47B ($600M x 0.79) + a mid-cycle AI-systems contribution ~$0.3-0.4B = ~$2.6B. FY2026E last_fcf of $2,585M therefore sits AT mid-cycle for the enlarged company, not above it; the sanity-check 'peak_fcf' ratio of 2.0x compares the post-Juniper company with the pre-Juniper median. The peak extrapolation was in the projected margin path (19.5% pre-SBC plateau, 2pp above HPE's best standalone year), which is what the 2026-09-29 fix pass removed.

equity_bridge.item: Debt benefiting Financial Services, net of FS cash (interest already charged above EBIT as Financing interest)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 10-K: debt benefiting FS $11.6B less FS cash $727M, balance date 2025-10-31; financing receivables were flat FY2025 -> Q3 FY2026 ($9,542M -> $9,701M) so the allocation is carried. HPEFS is a 7x-levered captive whose post-interest earnings sit inside EBITDA; deducting its debt in net debt would charge the same $500M/yr twice.

equity_bridge.item: Series C mandatory convertible preferred dividends to conversion (Sept 2027)
equity_bridge.note: 7.625% on $1.5B = $116M/yr; the preferred shares themselves are in the 1,449M diluted count.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management FY2027 framework (revenue +13-17%, press release 2026-09-02), taken just below the midpoint; not a historical CAGR. Decelerates to 2.5% terminal over ten years. Retained after the 2026-09-29 fix pass because it is the guided year backed by a contracted backlog; the fade beyond FY2027 now reverts to the through-cycle rate above.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 9.0% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 4.9% (84% divergence). The equity series is inflated by the $1.5B Series C preferred issued Sept 2024 and by Juniper purchase accounting; it is not a growth signal. EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are null because FY2020 and FY2025 are both loss/negative years (FY2020 COVID restructuring; FY2025 Juniper deal costs), so no meaningful endpoint pair exists.
historical_growth.notes: Windows: 3yr = FY2022->FY2025, 5yr = FY2020->FY2025, all post the 2015 HP Inc separation and 2017 spin-offs so no basis break is spanned; FY2025 includes 4 months of Juniper. Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less equity-award withholding; interest income not stripped, net-debt every year): FY2020 -457, FY2021 2,958, FY2022 1,027, FY2023 1,066, FY2024 1,460, FY2025 -305. Reported FCF over the same years: -143, 3,369, 1,471, 1,600, 1,974, 627. SBC plus withholding has risen from $314M (FY2020) to $932M (FY2025) and ~$1.2B (FY2026E) while reported FCF went sideways until FY2026, so a growing share of the pre-Juniper 'cash generation' was paid for in stock; the FY2026-27 step-up in FCF is the first time the owner series moves decisively.
historical_growth.through_cycle_window: FY2018 (30,852) -> FY2025 (34,296), continuing operations after the Nov-2015 HP Inc separation and the 2017 DXC/Micro Focus spin-offs; FY2025 carries four months of Juniper. Pre-Juniper FY2018 -> FY2024 (30,127) is -0.4%. The sanity check's -4.2% spans the basis break and is not used.
historical_growth.through_cycle_ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC EBITDA (GAAP EBITDA + SBC, CSV) / revenue, post-spin FY2018-24: 15.0, 14.0, 9.5, 14.8, 12.8, 17.6, 17.2 -> median 14.8%, best two years ~17.4%. Bear plateau = median; base plateau 18.0% = best standalone years + ~0.6pp net Juniper mix/synergy after AI-server dilution.

base.narrative: FY2027 growth 14% (guide 13-17%) as the AI-systems backlog ($5.9B) converts, then a fast fade - 5%, 3%, 2.5% - to 2.0% terminal, HPE's clean through-cycle organic rate (+1.5% FY2018-25, -0.4% pre-Juniper) plus a little Networking mix. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 18.5% in FY2027 (mgmt 14-15% non-GAAP OP + ~4.3% depreciation, less normalised restructuring), then drifting to a MID-CYCLE 18.0% plateau: FY2023-24 standalone ~17.4% plus Juniper mix and partial synergy, net of AI-server mix dilution. Cash tax ramps 17% -> 21% as the non-deductible Juniper amortisation shield and remaining credits run off. WACC 10% (structural premium, see wacc_rationale). Cap multiple 15x FCF (Gordon at 10%/2.0% is 12.8x, so the cap does not bind; the 10.8x EV/EBITDA exit cap does not bind either).

bull.narrative: Top of the FY2027 guide (17%) and a longer AI cycle: sovereign/enterprise AI orders keep the backlog growing, Juniper+Aruba cross-sell pushes Networking past 30% of revenue at 22%+ segment margins, GreenLake recurring revenue compounds; growth 9%/6%/4% then 3% terminal. Full $600M synergy plus the Catalyst cost programme lift pre-SBC EBITDA to a 20% plateau (was 21% before the 2026-09-29 mid-cycle fix; 20% is HPE's best standalone year plus the full synergy with no mix dilution). SBC as a share of revenue drifts down to 1.8% as revenue outgrows grants.

bear.narrative: FY2027 lands below the guide (8%) as AI-systems deliveries slip on GPU/HBM supply and export-control friction, then an AI-capex pause in FY2028-29 takes revenue down 3% in FY2029 while Dell's scale-at-thin-margin strategy forces HPE to chase volume; growth settles at 1.5% (below the through-cycle 1.5-2% because the AI piece unwinds). Pre-SBC EBITDA reverts to the post-spin standalone median of 15% (FY2018-24), i.e. synergies are consumed by commoditisation and a weaker Networking mix. SBC does not fall with revenue. No solvency stress: leverage stays under 2x, so the bear is a margin-and-cycle case, not a balance-sheet case.

scenario_narratives.base: HPE's axes are (1) whether the AI-systems backlog converts at the mid-to-high-teens Cloud & AI margin management is protecting rather than the ~20% gross margin Dell accepts for volume, (2) how much of the $600M Juniper synergy reaches the P&L by FY2028 while Networking holds 22% segment margins, and (3) how far the record Q3 FY2026 gross margin mean-reverts once AI server mix rises. Base takes the FY2027 framework (14% growth, 14-15% non-GAAP OP margin) at face value and then treats FY2026-27 as the high point of the cycle rather than the new floor: growth fades to 2.5% and margins plateau at 19.5% pre-SBC, about a point above the FY2023-24 pre-Juniper level, which is what a partly-delivered synergy net of mix dilution looks like.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI infrastructure demand proves multi-year rather than a two-year buildout, the sovereign/enterprise skew keeps HPE's AI margins above hyperscaler-heavy peers, and Juniper turns HPE into a credible number-two to Cisco with networking above 30% of revenue and more than half of profit. Synergies land in full, restructuring stops recurring, and the company compounds at 12% then 8% with pre-SBC EBITDA at 21%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The AI capex cycle pauses in FY2028-29, hyperscaler-style pricing bleeds into enterprise AI systems, Juniper integration and the Tunney Act overhang cost engineering talent and channel share, and the business reverts to the FY2019-24 pattern: low-single-digit growth, 15-16% pre-SBC EBITDA, SBC rising as a share of revenue. Because the balance sheet is sound the equity is worth roughly half the price, not zero.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the valuation rests on a cycle-peak year (record GM, +35% acquisition-driven revenue, stock up 3x from the 52-week low) and the bear axis - an AI-capex pause plus server commoditisation - is a normal industry cycle, not a tail event; no going-concern element, so it is not raised further. Bull cut to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold at once: a multi-year AI cycle, full synergy delivery, and margin discipline surviving Dell's volume strategy. Base 50%. Weights unchanged in the 2026-09-29 fix pass: the cycle risk is now also carried in the mid-cycle margin paths and the WACC premium, and raising the bear weight on top would charge it three times.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a strict basis: SBC plus net-share-settlement withholding expensed (~2.6% of revenue, share count flat), capex net of lease-equipment proceeds, working capital charged on growth, cash tax ramped to 21%, and the captive-finance debt charged once (its interest is above EBIT, so its debt is added back in the bridge). SANITY-CHECK FIX 2026-09-29: the first build of this valuation extrapolated the FY2026-27 cycle high - a 19.5% pre-SBC EBITDA plateau (2pp above HPE's best standalone year, 4.7pp above its post-spin median of 14.8%) and a growth fade above HPE's own -0.4% to +1.5% organic through-cycle record - and tripped the multiples sanity check (implied P/B 3.0x, EV/EBITDA 57x on the FY2025 deal-cost trough denominator). It was rebuilt mid-cycle: base margin plateau 18.0% (bull 20%, bear 15%), the guided FY2027 growth year retained but fading to 2.0% terminal, WACC raised from 9% to 10% with named cyclicality, regulatory/integration and supplier-concentration premia, and EV/EBITDA exit caps (7.0x/10.8x/13.4x) tested per scenario - none binds because the Gordon terminal values already sit at 5.4-8.5x post-SBC EBITDA. The weighted value fell ~26% (bridge in reconciliation). One residual is documented rather than forced: implied P/B ~2.1x still exceeds the 1.93x historical bound, because HPE's 1x-book decade was a 5-10% ROE business and the post-Juniper company is not. The FY2025 loss and the record Q3 FY2026 remain treated as discontinuity artefacts; terminal value capped at 15x FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Sanity-check residual: implied P/B ~2.1x vs the 10yr 1.93x bound; the valuation assumes post-Juniper earnings power (mid-cycle ~$4B unlevered owner FCF on ~$27B book) is durable, which HPE's pre-Juniper history does not evidence
AI-capex cyclicality: the fastest-growing, highest-margin revenue is tied to sovereign/cloud/enterprise AI buildouts that can pause; the bear case is a normal cycle, not a tail
Margin mean-reversion: Q3 FY2026 non-GAAP GM 40.4% is a record; the base already assumes drift back to an 18% pre-SBC EBITDA plateau, but the post-spin median is 14.8%
Juniper synergy and integration execution ($600M by FY2028), plus residual Tunney Act state-AG review of the DOJ settlement
Captive-finance treatment: $11.6B of 'debt benefiting FS' is a management allocation (7.0x assumed D/E), disclosed annually; if the FY2026 10-K changes the basis the bridge moves
SBC/withholding cost has doubled with the share price; a further re-rating raises the cash cost of net-share settlement
Cash tax: HPE's 15% non-GAAP rate is below the 17-21% modelled on EBIT; Pillar Two and US R&D capitalisation could push it higher still

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 19.84-65.65; regular-session close, not after-hours
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1645590) via research/HPE/Reports/HPE_Metrics.csv and HPE.duckdb; 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 (filed 2026-09-03) for the balance sheet, diluted shares, SBC, withholding, net capex and the non-GAAP reconciliation; FY2025 10-K (filed 2025-12-18) for debt benefiting Financial Services, FS cash, financing interest and operating lease liability; press release 2026-09-02 (8-K ex-99.1) for Q4 FY2026, FY2026 and FY2027 guidance

exit_multiple_cap.basis: EV / (EBITDA less SBC), the sanity-check basis; caps set from the 10yr historical table ex artefacts and tested against the Gordon terminal value (min(Gordon TV, cap x terminal post-SBC EBITDA)). The engine's terminal_cap_multiple is in FCF terms, so each EV/EBITDA cap is also expressed as its FCF-multiple equivalent for comparison.

bear.cap_source: 10yr min post-spin (FY2018 6.9x, FY2023 7.1x); FY2016 3.7x excluded as a pre-DXC/Micro Focus basis break

bull.cap_source: 10yr max excluding FY2025 31.6x (deal-cost trough EBITDA denominator); FY2020 13.4x

exit_multiple_cap.note: terminal_cap_multiple stays at 15x FCF in every scenario because it is tighter than any EV/EBITDA cap; at 10% WACC the Gordon multiples are 11.9x (bear, g 1.5%), 12.8x (base, g 2.0%) and 14.7x (bull, g 3.0%), so neither cap binds.

prior_version.note: First build of the same day, before the sanity-check fix pass (tripped: implied P/B 3.00x, EV/EBITDA 57.2x on the FY2025 trough denominator).

bridge.item: Mid-cycle margins: base plateau 19.5% -> 18.0%, bull 21% -> 20%, bear 16% -> 15% (priority 1, peak extrapolation)
Growth fade to through-cycle: base 8/5/4/3.5 -> 5/3/2.5, terminal 2.5% -> 2.0%; bull and bear fades trimmed likewise (priority 3, guided FY2027 year kept)
EV/EBITDA exit caps per scenario (priority 4) - non-binding, Gordon TVs already below 7.0x/10.8x/13.4x
Anchors (price, net debt, shares, guidance) - unchanged, same day

sanity_check_response.trip: Implied P/B 3.00x (>1.5 x 10yr max 1.28x) and EV/EBITDA 57.2x (>1.5 x 10yr max 31.6x) on the first build (base $56.02).
sanity_check_response.root_cause: Two things. (a) Denominator artefact: the check divides EV by FY2025 GAAP EBITDA less SBC ($1,657M), a GAAP-operating-loss year with $458M Juniper deal costs and four months of Juniper; on FY2026E post-SBC EBITDA (~$7.7B) the first build implied ~12x. (b) Genuine peak extrapolation in the margin path: the base plateau of 19.5% pre-SBC EBITDA was 2pp above HPE's best standalone year and 4.7pp above the post-spin median, and the growth fade sat above HPE's -0.4% to +1.5% organic through-cycle record.
sanity_check_response.fix_applied: Priority 1 mid-cycle margins (base 18.0%, bull 20.0%, bear 15.0%); priority 2 WACC 9.0% -> 10.0% with named premia; priority 3 growth fade to through-cycle (guided FY2027 kept; clean window FY2018-25, not the basis-break -4.2%); priority 4 EV/EBITDA exit caps recorded per scenario (non-binding).
sanity_check_response.expected_after_fix: EV/EBITDA on the FY2025 denominator ~43x, inside the 47.4x bound. P/B ~2.1x vs the 1.93x bound: residual, deliberately not forced. HPE's 0.7-1.3x book decade was a 5-10% ROE business; the post-Juniper company earns ~$4B mid-cycle unlevered owner FCF on ~$27B book. Forcing P/B below 1.93x would mean base IV under ~$36 - valuing the enlarged company at the pre-Juniper return on book - on a model already ~37% below the market price with mid-cycle margins, through-cycle growth and a 10% WACC.
sanity_check_response.not_changed: Weights 25/50/25, SBC/withholding path, capex 5% net, working-capital capture -6%, cash-tax ramp, captive-finance bridge, flat diluted share count. Evidence that would move them: FY2026 10-K restating debt benefiting FS; a FY2027 guide cut; SBC/withholding running above 2.6% of revenue.
